title: Incident Comms Template Drafts (Statuspage + Console) — tone guide + sample updates
content:
Working doc. Expect rough edges.

Purpose
- Draft/iterate customer-facing incident updates for Statuspage (public) + Console linking.
- Provide a tone guide + fill-in-the-blank blocks that incident-bot can generate.
- Reduce time-to-first-update (TTFU) without over-promising, leaking sensitive details, or causing extra on-call load.

Audience
- Public Statuspage readers (customers + prospects).
- Support/CS using these updates as the “single source” for external comms.

Non-goals
- No internal debugging details, no customer names, no capacity allocation specifics.
- No commitments to exact ETAs unless we are highly confident and approved.

Tone guide (draft v0.6)
- Be direct, calm, and specific about customer impact.
- Prefer “We are investigating reports of…” over “We are aware…”
- Always state: what’s impacted + which regions/components + what users may experience.
- Avoid implying data exposure unless confirmed and approved by Security/Legal.
- Avoid precise SLAs/credits language (“SLA impacted”, “credits will be applied”) on Statuspage.
  - Use: “We’ll share details in the post-incident summary.”
- Avoid absolutes early (“fully mitigated”) unless metrics confirm.
- Don’t copy/paste internal incident taxonomy (e.g., “scheduler flapped”, “KV cache churn”) into public updates.
- Use consistent verbs across phases:
  - Investigating: “investigating”, “working to identify”, “reviewing metrics”.
  - Identified: “identified the cause”, “confirming the scope”, “working on mitigation.”
  - Mitigating: “applying mitigation”, “rolling back”, “failing over”, “reducing load”.
  - Monitoring: “monitoring to confirm recovery”, “traffic has stabilized”.
  - Resolved: “issue is resolved”, “services operating normally”.

What every update should include (checklist)
- Component(s) impacted (Hosted API / Streaming / Embeddings / Reranking / Console) + region(s) when applicable.
- Customer symptoms (e.g., elevated error rate, increased latency, streaming disconnects).
- Our current state (investigating / identified / mitigating / monitoring / resolved).
- What users can do (retry guidance, temporary workaround) ONLY if it’s safe and not misleading.
- Next update timing:
  - Investigating: within 30 min.
  - Identified/Mitigating: within 30–60 min, or sooner if status changes.
  - Monitoring: provide cadence (“next update in ~60 minutes or sooner”).

Words/phrases to avoid (public)
- “bug”, “negligence”, “human error” (unless later in summary and approved)
- “we guarantee”, “SLA”, “credit”, “breach”, “compromised” (requires Security/Legal)
- “only a small number of customers” (often wrong and invites disputes)
- “all regions unaffected” (unless verified by dashboards)

Good phrases
- “some requests may fail”
- “a subset of requests” (if we have data)
- “elevated error rates / increased latency”
- “intermittent” (only if truly intermittent)
- “We’re seeing recovery in metrics, and are monitoring to confirm stability.”

Approval notes (draft)
- Sev0/Sev1: Support lead approval step is recommended if update includes workaround, expected recovery window, or scope change that may conflict with ticket guidance.
- Security-related language: requires Security + Legal (Naomi Feldman + Michael Grant or delegate).

----------------------------------------
TEMPLATES (status update blocks)

[1] INVESTIGATING — generic (v3)
Title suggestion: “Degraded performance for <Component> in <Region>” or “Elevated errors for <Component>”
Body:
"We are investigating an issue affecting <Component> in <Region>. Some customers may experience <symptom(s): elevated error rates / increased latency / streaming disconnects>.

We are working to identify the cause and will provide another update within <30 minutes> or sooner as we learn more." 

Notes
- Keep “impact” sentence first.
- If scope unknown, omit region: “in some regions.” (but try to confirm quickly).

[2] INVESTIGATING — when partial/uncertain scope (v2)
"We are investigating reports of issues with <Component>. Customers may see <symptoms>. We are reviewing metrics to confirm the scope and impact.

Next update within <30 minutes> or sooner." 

[3] IDENTIFIED — root cause class but not internals (v4)
"We have identified the cause of the issue affecting <Component> in <Region>. We are working on mitigation and continue to monitor customer impact.

Next update within <60 minutes> or sooner." 

Optional add-on if useful and safe:
- “Requests may succeed on retry.” (only if verified)
- “We are routing traffic to alternate capacity.” (avoid naming vendors/regions if it reveals constraints)

[4] MITIGATING — rollback/failover style (v5)
"We are applying mitigation for the issue affecting <Component> in <Region>, and we are seeing early signs of recovery in <errors/latency/stream stability>.

We will continue to monitor and provide another update within <60 minutes> or sooner." 

[5] MONITORING — recovery observed (v3)
"Mitigation has been applied and <Component> in <Region> is recovering. We are monitoring to confirm stability before marking this incident fully resolved.

Next update within <60 minutes> or sooner." 

[6] RESOLVED — concise (v4)
"This incident has been resolved and <Component> in <Region> is operating normally.

We will publish a post-incident summary with additional details and follow-ups." 

[7] RESOLVED — if workaround used / failover occurred (v2)
"This incident has been resolved. <Component> in <Region> is operating normally.

We mitigated the issue by <high-level action: rolling back a change / shifting traffic / restarting a subsystem> and have put follow-up actions in place to prevent recurrence. We will publish a post-incident summary with more details." 

----------------------------------------
COMPONENT-SPECIFIC TEMPLATES

[A] STREAMING — disconnects / stalled streams (v3)
Investigating:
"We are investigating an issue affecting Streaming responses in <Region>. Some customers may experience stream interruptions, disconnects, or stalled responses.

We are working to identify the cause and will provide another update within 30 minutes or sooner." 

Mitigating:
"We are applying mitigation for the Streaming interruption issue in <Region>. We are seeing improvement in stream stability and disconnect rates.

We will continue monitoring and provide another update within 60 minutes or sooner." 

[B] EMBEDDINGS — elevated errors (v3)
Investigating:
"We are investigating an issue affecting Embeddings requests in <Region>. Some customers may see elevated error rates or timeouts.

Next update within 30 minutes or sooner." 

Resolved:
"The issue affecting Embeddings requests in <Region> has been resolved and service is operating normally.

We will publish a post-incident summary with additional details and follow-ups." 

[C] HOSTED API — latency-only degradation (v2)
"We are investigating increased latency for Hosted API requests in <Region>. Some requests may take longer than usual to complete.

We are working to mitigate and will provide another update within 30 minutes or sooner." 

Note: Only use if dashboards confirm widespread latency impact. Avoid triggering status changes on minor p95 blips.

[D] CONSOLE — read-only / login issues (v2)
"We are investigating an issue affecting the Redwood Console. Some customers may experience <login failures / delayed metrics / errors viewing dashboards>.

The Hosted API is <not impacted / impacted separately as noted>. Next update within 30 minutes or sooner." 

----------------------------------------
REGION WORDING GUIDANCE (draft)
- Use public region labels consistently (e.g., “US East”, “US West”, “EU Central”).
- If multiple regions affected, list explicitly when possible: “US East and EU Central.”
- If only a subset of traffic in a region is affected, say “some customers in US East” (not “subset of customers” with no region).

----------------------------------------
EXAMPLES FROM RECENT INCIDENTS (EDITED)

Example 1 — Partial Streaming degradation (US East) — what we wish we posted earlier (based on 2025-11-07 postmortem)

Investigating (better v1):
"We are investigating an issue affecting Streaming responses in US East. Some customers may experience stream interruptions or stalled responses.

We are working to identify the cause and will provide another update within 30 minutes or sooner." 

Identified (better v1):
"We have identified the cause of the Streaming interruption issue in US East. We are working on mitigation and continue monitoring stream stability.

Next update within 60 minutes or sooner." 

Mitigating (better v1):
"We are applying mitigation for the Streaming issue in US East and are seeing improvement in disconnect rates.

We will continue monitoring and provide another update within 60 minutes or sooner." 

Resolved (better v1):
"This incident has been resolved and Streaming in US East is operating normally.

We will publish a post-incident summary with additional details and follow-ups." 

Notes:
- Avoid “API down” if only Streaming was affected.
- Mention symptoms customers actually saw (disconnects/stalls) not internal terms.

Example 2 — Misclassified Embeddings impact (learning example)

Problem statement (internal): status page said “API Degraded” but customers reported embeddings-only failures.

Public wording that would reduce disputes:
"We are investigating an issue affecting Embeddings requests in US West. Some customers may see elevated error rates.

Other Hosted API capabilities (Chat/Completions) appear unaffected at this time, and we are continuing to verify." 

Note: Only include “other capabilities unaffected” if we have dashboard confirmation and we’re confident. Otherwise omit.

Example 3 — Multi-component incident (gateway) — careful scope

Investigating:
"We are investigating an issue affecting Hosted API requests in EU Central. Some customers may experience elevated error rates across multiple capabilities (Chat/Completions/Embeddings).

We are working to identify the cause and will provide another update within 30 minutes or sooner." 

Mitigating:
"We are applying mitigation and are seeing improvement in error rates for Hosted API requests in EU Central. Some intermittent errors may continue while recovery completes.

Next update within 60 minutes or sooner." 

----------------------------------------
VARIANTS / EDIT HISTORY (notes)

2025-10-28 (Wei) — v0.1
- First pass templates. Too wordy. Missing next-update cadence.

2025-11-02 (Christine) — v0.3
- Added streaming-specific language (“disconnects/stalled”) after runtime feedback.
- Added checklist + words to avoid.

2025-11-10 (Dev Patel) — v0.4
- Strong preference: stop saying “subset of customers” without region/scope.
- Ask: include Support-safe workaround line only when verified.

2025-11-12 (Michael Grant) — v0.5
- Remove “SLA impacted” phrasing.
- Do not mention “data exposure” speculation.

2025-11-18 (Rafael) — v0.6
- Added “monitoring” phase block.
- Added explicit instruction: impact sentence first.

----------------------------------------
OPEN QUESTIONS (to resolve before moving to Confluence ‘canonical’)
- Should we always include “next update within X minutes” or allow “we will update as we learn more” for low-sev? (Support prefers always include time.)
- When/how to mention failover across regions without implying capacity constraints?
- Dedicated/Private wording: do we show components publicly, or only “Dedicated Control Plane” at aggregate? (Kira + Product decision pending.)

TODO (for incident-bot generation)
- Add slots: <component>, <capability>, <region>, <symptoms>, <next_update_minutes>.
- Include optional “Other capabilities appear unaffected” toggle gated by dashboard check.
- Add approval gating for sev0/sev1 updates with workaround language.

Quick reminder for Comms Lead (paste into #incidents)
- First public update: within 30 min, even if the message is “investigating”.
- Keep it short, impact-first.
- Update status components precisely (Streaming vs Hosted API vs Embeddings).
- Coordinate with Support before publishing workaround language.
